outline: 550 The Derivative of a Linear Function

examples.solution_text:
The temperature increases by $15.6^{\circ}\text{C}$ over $3.5$ minutes. The average rate is the gradient of the secant joining the two marked points.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Average rate}&=\frac{26.8-11.2}{5-1.5}\\&=\frac{15.6}{3.5}\\&\approx4.46^{\circ}\text{C/min}\end{aligned}$

The answer is rounded to $2$ decimal places.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Rate}&=\frac{24-84}{5-0}\\&=\frac{-60}{5}\\&=-12\text{ L/min}\end{aligned}$

The negative sign means the volume decreases by $12$ litres each minute. The rate is constant because the graph is a straight line.

The object travels $33$ metres during the $3$-second interval.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Average speed}&=\frac{D(4)-D(1)}{4-1}\\&=\frac{36-3}{3}\\&=11\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}$

This is the gradient of the secant between the marked points; it does not imply a constant speed throughout the interval.

examples.derivation: The plotted curve gives f(-3)=9 and f(2)=-1. The secant gradient is (-1-9)/(2-(-3))=-10/5=-2. Its equation y=-2x+3 matches both drawn secant endpoints. The solution's horizontal change 5 and vertical change -10 are correct.

The marked points coincide with the curve endpoints of the relevant segments. Temperature change is 26.8-11.2=15.6 degrees Celsius; elapsed time is 5-1.5=3.5 minutes. Their quotient is 4.457142857..., giving 4.46 degrees Celsius per minute to two decimal places.
The straight line joins (0,84) and (5,24). Its gradient is (24-84)/(5-0)=-60/5=-12 litres per minute. The negative sign indicates decreasing volume; the straight line establishes a constant rate.

The plotted rule D(t)=2t^2+t gives D(1)=3 and D(4)=36 and increases throughout the stated interval. Distance travelled is 36-3=33 metres over 4-1=3 seconds, so average speed is 11 metres per second. This secant gradient does not imply constant speed.
